- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If 30-day forecast shows strong upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion within 10–15 days, reduce forecast slope.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 5+ consecutive days, model tends to overfit recent momentum; dampen forecast volatility.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust later days downward if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, consider “price exhaustion” heuristic: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts.
